question: Which of the following article of the Indian Constitution is related with Admission or establishment of new States?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 2** of the **Indian Constitution** empowers Parliament to admit new states into the Union of India or establish new states.
 
• This provision grants the Parliament the authority to create or incorporate new states into the Indian territory, ensuring flexibility in territorial expansion.
 
• The admission or establishment of new states under **Article 2** is subject to the terms and conditions specified by Parliament.
 
• It is distinct from **Article 3**, which deals with changes in the boundaries or names of existing states. Article 2 strictly pertains to the inclusion of new states in the Union.
 
• **Examples** of states admitted under Article 2 include the inclusion of Sikkim as a full-fledged state in the Indian Union in **1975**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 2 vs Article 3:**

 
 
• **Article 2:** Deals with the admission or establishment of new states in the Union of India. It is applicable for territories that were not previously part of India.
 
• **Article 3:** Pertains to the reorganization of existing states, such as altering state boundaries, merging states, or changing state names.
 
 
 
• **Sikkim's Inclusion:**
 
 
• Sikkim was initially a protectorate under India and became a state under **Article 2** in **1975** after a referendum.
 
• This marked a significant event in India's territorial expansion post-independence.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• After India's independence in **1947**, various princely states and territories joined India through legal and constitutional provisions like **Article 2**.
 
• Examples include the inclusion of French territories like Pondicherry and Portuguese territories like Goa into the Indian Union.
 
 
 
• **Role of Parliament:**
 
 
• Parliament holds the supreme authority in deciding the terms and conditions for admitting new states under Article 2.
 
• Any such admission requires the passage of a law in Parliament, ensuring democratic oversight.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Constitutional Flexibility:** Article 2 allows India to incorporate new territories or states, demonstrating the Constitution's adaptability to geopolitical changes.
 
• **Global Examples:** Similar provisions exist in other federal systems worldwide, such as the United States, which can admit new states into its union.
 
• **Legal Framework:** The inclusion of new states requires careful deliberation in Parliament, ensuring adherence to constitutional principles and democratic processes.
 
• **Statehood Process:** Territories aspiring for statehood typically undergo extensive negotiations and legal frameworks before being admitted under Article 2.
